findings.title: Authenticated upload retains process-crash and CPU-exhaustion paths
findings.actual_conditions: Crafted multipart text-field names reach vulnerable Multer parsing only after a valid active session, completed password change/onboarding, and X-Requested-With. File-size and gateway body limits do not prevent the small-field attacks.
findings.reachability: Authenticated reachable; unauthenticated reachability not established.
findings.impact: Availability loss of the shared API process; no RCE claim.
findings.confidence: high for static reachability; not reproduced
findings.reason: The stated test cohort contains only the private operator OWNER, with no public signup or untrusted authenticated users.
findings.followup: Priority debt before opening authenticated access to untrusted users. If that condition changes, the smallest non-upgrade containment is to block POST /api/bff/arquivos at the public gateway. Future narrowly scoped dependency maintenance should resolve Multer to >=2.4.0 with Nest compatibility validation.

findings.title: Critical proxy-addr advisory prerequisite is absent
findings.actual_conditions: The advisory requires an incorrectly configured IPv6 trust subnet that also matches IPv4 clients. This application configures numeric trust proxy=1. Express compiles numeric trust into a hop-count predicate, bypassing subnet compilation.
findings.reachability: Installed vulnerable version; advisory-specific exploit condition absent in reviewed configuration.
findings.followup: Keep the patched-version debt recorded. Do not label this configuration as a demonstrated critical spoofing or RCE path.

findings.title: Remaining Multer advisories do not match the upload configuration
findings.audit_severity: high aggregate; individual advisories high, moderate and low
findings.actual_conditions: The descriptor-leak and orphaned-file advisories require Multer diskStorage. This route uses default memoryStorage and receives arquivo.buffer; application disk writes occur after parsing. The size-limit race requires an asynchronous fileFilter, which is absent. Application storage also rechecks buffer length.
findings.confidence: high; no application MulterModule, custom storage or fileFilter configuration found in public source

findings.title: qs parser is public, but neither audited exploit chain is established

actual_conditions.parser_boundary: Global extended URL-encoded parsing runs before surface authentication. JSON has an explicit 1 MiB limit; URL-encoded parsing independently inherits body-parser's 100 KiB default, 1000-parameter limit and depth 32.
actual_conditions.comma_advisory: Requires comma=true. Neither application configuration nor body-parser enables it; qs defaults to false.
actual_conditions.isBuffer_advisory: Requires hostile parsed objects to reach qs.stringify. body-parser permits prototype-named own properties, so the hostile shape is possible, but no qs.stringify call or parse-to-stringify round trip was found in application source. Parsing alone does not establish this advisory's throw.

findings.confidence: high for configured options; medium-high for absence of a complete transitive stringify path
findings.followup: Retain qs >=6.16.0 as scoped dependency debt; extended=true alone is not evidence of either reported exploit.

findings.title: Prisma configuration merge vulnerability lacks a request path
findings.audit_severity: high, propagated across three package entries
findings.actual_conditions: The advisory requires matching cyclic object graphs supplied to merge operations; plain JSON cannot create those cycles. Public application source imports PrismaClient from @prisma/client, not Prisma CLI configuration or deepmerge-ts. Reviewed migration code queries migration state; CLI migration invocation is operator startup work.
findings.confidence: high for advisory prerequisite; medium-high for absence of an HTTP-to-config path
findings.followup: Configuration/tooling dependency debt. No broad Prisma upgrade or unvalidated major-version override is required by this diagnostic.

findings.title: source-map-js has no identified untrusted map consumer
findings.actual_conditions: Exploitation requires consuming attacker-controlled indexed source maps with excessive section offsets. No SourceMapConsumer, SourceNode, source-map-js import, map-processing endpoint or equivalent request path was found in application source.
findings.inventory_caveat: The lockfile marks this package devOptional and links it through tooling/optional magicast paths. The supplied production-image audit nevertheless reports it present; it must not be dismissed as absent.
findings.confidence: medium-high; transitive runtime consumers were not dynamically traced
findings.followup: Scoped package/tooling debt toward >=1.2.2; reassess if untrusted map processing is introduced.

findings.title: Tunnel proxy hop may reduce client-IP accuracy
findings.actual_conditions: With trust proxy=1 and Nginx appending its immediate peer to X-Forwarded-For, req.ip selects that appended peer. An additional tunnel hop may therefore group clients under the tunnel/Docker peer. Attacker-controlled earlier header entries alone do not establish spoofing through this gateway configuration.
findings.impact: Possible shared recovery throttling and reduced audit IP accuracy; this is separate from the proxy-addr subnet CVE. Login throttling in current source is keyed by email.
findings.confidence: medium; actual tunnel headers were not inspected
findings.followup: Verify real client-IP attribution before relying on per-IP controls beyond this private operator test.

decision.scope: ST-CON-01 targeted dependency diagnostic for a short-lived public HTTPS operator test
decision.rationale: No unauthenticated exploit chain for the audited dependency advisories was established. A concrete authenticated Multer availability risk remains, bounded here by the stated operator-only account cohort.
conditions: Tunnel targets the same gateway; API, databases, cache and Evolution remain unpublished.
Only private operator credentials and synthetic tenant data are used.
The stated production NODE_ENV, Secure cookies and exact HTTPS origin are applied. channels Compose defaults to development, so the override matters.
Exposure is temporary and stopped after the authorized test.

evidence_and_limits.count_interpretation: Eight affected package entries, not eight independent remotely exploitable flaws; Nest and Prisma entries include propagated dependency effects.
evidence_and_limits.version_basis: Exact lockfile versions plus supplied audit from the actual production image. Image-to-lockfile concordance was not independently rechecked.
evidence_and_limits.validation: Read-only source/configuration analysis and current primary advisory/maintainer sources; no runtime commands, payloads or exploit probes.
evidence_and_limits.attack_simulation_status: Not run under this diagnostic's explicit read-only restriction; future isolated validation can confirm the authenticated Multer failure and tunnel header behavior.
parent_supplied_not_reverified: Actual secret state, synthetic-only database state and private account cohort
Webhook-token rotation and live logging/redaction proof
Current running environment values and final proof matrix
evidence_and_limits.independent_external_proof: Real Meta authorization, device pairing and IN/OUT remain independent integration evidence, not dependency findings.

governance.routing_result: go; blocked=false; formal-review critique; declared gpt-6.1-sol/max
